Subject: Subprocessor certification needs and SCCs sequencing

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. LegalOps pulled together a short list of questions so we can close the DPA and verify our routing requirements for EU patient data. High-level asks: 

- Can you provide a current subprocessor inventory with certification status (ISO27001 / SOC 2) and whether any subprocessors route traffic outside the EEA?
- We need a proposed sequencing for SCCs + any TIA/DTIA evidence you can provide for your third-party infra (esp. cache/edge vendors).
- If a UK addendum is required for UK-resident subjects, please note where an IDTA fallback will be used.

Target timeline from MedGroup: execute DPA + routing attestations within 3 weeks (we have a board compliance checkpoint on 11/8). Appreciate a clear M.A.P. with owners so LegalOps can slot the items into our procurement sprint.

Attaching our internal evidence checklist for reference (lightweight).

Best,
Anna Rossi
Senior Legal Operations
MedGroup Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Subprocessor certification needs and SCCs sequencing

Hi Anna —

Thanks — clear asks and an achievable timeline. Quick reply with proposed approach and owners: 

1) Subprocessor inventory (owner: Rishi / ops): we will export the latest matrix and flag certifications + geographic routing for each entry. Expect versioned CSV by EOD Monday (attached: subprocessor_matrix_v2.csv).

2) SCCs / TIA sequencing (owner: Kimberly / privacy counsel): Kimberly will provide mapping that pairs each family of processors (edge cache, metrics, storage) with the applicable SCC cluster and indicate where TIA output/evidence exists (e.g., contractual addendums, attestation letters). We can mark items that require further evidence collection.

3) UK addendum fallback (owner: Laura / legal): Laura will confirm if MedGroup needs an IDTA or if the UK addendum + residual safeguards are sufficient for your processing. If an IDTA is needed we will propose a short alternate workflow (DocuSign cadence + evidence handoff).

4) M.A.P. (mutual action plan): I propose a 2-week sprint to assemble the documents, with check-ins Tues/Wed next week and a final DPA handoff on 11/5 to leave you time for the board review. If that works I’ll create a shared drive folder and a HubSpot deal task list.

Attached: subprocessor_matrix_v2.csv (stub), initial TIA mapping workbook placeholder (redwood_tia_mapping.xlsx stub).

If you prefer, we can lock in a 30-minute call Monday afternoon to walk the map.

On the technical side, note that Redwood supports automatic KV prefix caching which can be restricted by region — we can scope whether your EU-resident contexts ever hit non-EEA cache nodes and provide logs for sampling.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi / Anna — adding a few technical clarifications to ensure the TIA mapping is actionable for MedGroup's privacy team: 

- Edge/cache vendors: we will produce a matrix that shows whether a vendor operates EU-only endpoints or multi-region points-of-presence. For vendors that are multi-region we will flag the control as either (A) contractual restriction + routing assurance, (B) pseudonymization at rest, or (C) temporary onshore cache fallback.

- Logging / audit evidence: Redwood can export time-bounded audit slices (token-level latency & region-of-origin) to help you sample whether traffic touched non-EEA nodes. We’ll provide a template query and one sample CSV.

- SCCs vs UK IDTA: operationally, SCCs cover the EEA exit points; the UK addendum is needed only if processing of UK persons is in scope and the UK IDTA is our recommended fallback in markets where regulators insist on a dedicated instrument. Laura — if MedGroup confirms UK-resident scope, we should plan an IDTA parallel path that doesn't block DPA execution.

- Risk mitigations we can offer now: regional routing policies, KV cache TTL reduction, and an option for partial pseudonymization for sensitive fields prior to leaving the EU. Each mitigation will have a minor perf/cost tradeoff; I will annotate those in the mapping sheet.

I’ll take point on the mapping doc and will upload a populated workbook by Monday morning (PST).

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_tia_mapping.xlsx (will include tabs: vendor_routing, evidence_index, mitigation_costs)
